shipped_rows.title_o: Motivating voter turnout by invoking the self

blind_target.evidence_quote: An initial study analyzing two small‐scale field experiments argued that describing someone as a voter (noun) instead of one who votes (verb) increases turnout rates 11 to 14 points because the noun activates a person's social identity as a voter.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We find no evidence that this minor wording change increases turnout levels.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Abstract states the original positive noun-versus-verb turnout finding and this replication finds no evidence of the increase.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract clearly describes retesting the initial noun-versus-verb turnout claim, but it supplies no author, year, title, or citation for that initial study. The only supplied shipped original is the later large-scale study that challenged the claim, not the initial finding. The available abstract cannot establish the initial work's identity or whether that original appears under another citation.
luna_triage.omission_quote: An initial study analyzing two small‐scale field experiments argued that describing someone as a voter (noun) instead of one who votes (verb) increases turnout rates 11 to 14 points because the noun activates a person's social identity as a voter.
luna_triage.identity_quote: An initial study analyzing two small‐scale field experiments
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: A subsequent study analyzing a large‐scale field experiment challenged this claim and found no effect.

quality_gate: Luna is triage only. Independently establish actual empirical retesting and absence under ALL shipped identities/alternate reports. Read prior objections. No paper outcome is being requested.
